issues.issue: The provision cites "Section XDI", a section that does not exist in the Policy; the intended reference to Section XIII must be supplied by construction.

The retention figures in this Discovery Period table (e.g. $160,000 for Directors and Officers Liability) do not match the retentions set out in Item 9 of the Declarations ($0 / $100,000), leaving which retention governs Discovery Period Claims open.
"Financial Impairment" is defined in Section IV(I) solely as a status of the Company or a Subsidiary, yet this paragraph applies it to the acquiring entity, which is neither.

"The acquiring entity" is used with the definite article but is nowhere identified or defined, and the qualifier "only for Wrongful Acts involving the entity or entities set forth in Item 1" leaves the scope of that entity's coverage uncertain.
The stated expiration is written "0443/2009", which is not a date, so the end of the Policy Period cannot be read off the face of the item.

The $10,000,000 Total Policy Limit sits against Item 8, which sets separate Limits of Liability for five Insuring Agreements totalling more than $10,000,000, leaving the interaction of the aggregate cap and the individual limits to be worked out.

The footnote says Insuring Agreement (C) includes Securities Liability coverage and that a separate agreement is provided only if coverage is "excluded under Insuring Agreement (C)", yet the table also grants a separate $10,000,000 Securities Liability agreement, so the overlap with (C) must be construed.
Item 6 shows IRA/Keogh Liability as N/A with no limit or premium, while this item fixes a $5,000 retention for IRA/Keogh Claims, leaving it unclear whether such coverage exists at all.
The list of incorporated endorsements differs from the lists in the later Declarations amendments (c020 and c024), so which endorsements form part of the Policy is not settled by this item alone.

This clause makes the Declarations, Application, Policy and Endorsements the contract, while Section XVI(B) describes the entire agreement as the Policy, Application and written Endorsements without mentioning the Declarations.

The endorsement extending the Policy Period is made effective at 12:01 a.m. on 04/13/2009, the precise moment the previous Policy Period expired under Item 2, raising the question whether it operated before expiry.

Placing Vantus Bank first in Item 1 changes the identity of the "Named Insured" as defined in Section IV (the first named entity), which controls notice, cancellation and the Discovery Period election.

Coverage is conditioned on a limit, retention and premium being "set forth in the Declarations", yet Item 6 shows the retention for Insuring Agreement (A) as $0/N-A and gives (A) and (B) a single combined premium.
The carve-out "except for Loss the Company pays as indemnification" turns on actual payment, and its boundary against advanced but unreimbursed Defense Costs is not stated.

The closing sentence withdrawing coverage for "any loss arising from any act or omission by an Insured Person's estate, heirs, legal representatives, assigns, or spouse" is capable of being read to negate most of the grant it qualifies.

This clause confines the conversion trigger for the Discovery Period to Section XIII(C)(1)(b), while Section XIII(C)(2) states that the occurrence of any of the conversion events in (C)(1) — including Financial Impairment under (a) — shall not affect the right to purchase the Discovery Period.

The Discovery Period Activation endorsement lists separate amounts and premiums for each coverage, which sits awkwardly with this statement that the Discovery Period limit is part of and not in addition to the preceding Policy Year's limit.
"A written or oral demand for monetary damages or non-monetary relief" has no threshold of formality, so whether a letter, regulatory communication or informal demand is a Claim is genuinely open.

The Discovery Period Activation endorsement deletes and replaces this definition (c004) with one that adds "the acquiring entity" and drops the bank-Subsidiary limb, so two inconsistent definitions of Company appear in the instrument.
"Reasonable and necessary legal fees and expenses" is an undefined standard, and the exclusion of "overhead" has no stated boundary against billed disbursements.
"Leased Employee" and "Independent Contractor" are capitalised as defined terms, but Section IV contains no definition of either, so the carve-out from "Employee" has no stated content.
